title: Application of Decision Rules for Handling Class Imbalance in Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Replace argmax-of-posterior by a prior-corrected decision rule (posterior divided by class prior, globally or per pixel position) so rare classes are not ignored at inference.
adaptation: Zero training. Fit one logit bias per class (13 mIoU_rob classes plus splice) on out-of-fold logits from the existing module-grouped 5-fold roots, apply to the 5-seed ensemble. Position priors only for edge classes (edge_dark, frame_edge, border), not crack. Main target: splice (0.000, 4 test cells, worth +0.023 mIoU_rob at IoU 0.3).
min_experiment: Arm: per-class bias vector fitted by coordinate ascent on OOF mIoU_rob, applied to 5-seed ensemble; baseline: same ensemble with crack-only bias; metric test clean-49 mIoU_rob and splice IoU; kill if mIoU_rob gain < +0.01 or splice IoU < 0.05. Precede with per-class AP diagnostic on OOF logits.
evidence: R: street scenes, 20k frames: pedestrian instance recall +25%, info signs +23.4%, non-detection -61% / -38%.
prior_overlap: Partial: crack-only val-chosen logit bias already used in best ensemble; per-module thresholds failed. Per-class bias for all classes, chosen on OOF folds, never tested.
